entries.german:
Abt Heinrich von St. Gallen schenkt Ulrich von Gmünden und dessen Gemahlin und Kindern das Bürgerrecht der Stadt St. Gallen.

In a) nomine domini amen. Henricus dei gratia abbas monasterii sancti Galli 1 Omnibus intuentibus presens scriptum salutem in domino cum notitia subscriptorum. Noverint | universi, quos nosce fuerit oportunum, quod nos intuentes grata devotionis obsequia, que nobis nostroque monasterio vir discretus V olricus de Gemundin 2 inpendit plurimum et adhuc || conatur inpendere, nos eidem gratia dictorum servitiorum suorum, Mehtildi uxori sue filie Henrici quondam ministri ze Tufin 3, Bersino filio suo necnon omnibus pueris per ipsorum || commixitionem de cetera procreandis contulimus ac presentium testimonio litterarum damus tradimus et donamus liberum ac merum ius burgense sive civile in oppido nostro sancti Galli, quod vulgariter vris burger reht nuncupatur, cum omni iure libertate et ambitu eodem vocabulo conprehenso, volentes, ut memoratus V olricus, Mehtild. uxor sua, Bercinus filius eorum necnon etiam omnes et singuli pueri ipsorum b) utriusque sexus eodem iure gaudeant et utantur necnon conswetudine, sicut a predecessoribus nostris et a retroactis temporibus statutum et ordinatum est 4 feliciter et usque ad hec tempora inviolabiliter observatum, promittentes bona fide pro nobis nostrisque successoribus universis, memoratas personas tam in morte quam in vita in dieto iure burgensi illesos per omnia conservare. In cuius rei testimonium sigillum nostrum duximus presentibus apponendum. Datum et actum apud sanctum Gallum, anno domini millesimo CCC°IIII°. XVI. kal. septembr. Presentibus domino Egl. de Rosinberg 5, Walt, de Enwile 6, V oI. dicto Meldeli 7, VI. ministro oppidi sancti Galli 8, Wilderico et V olrico filio suo, Alb. dicto Blarrer, C. dicto Blarrer, H. dicto Blarrer, C. ministro Abbatiscelle 9, H. dicto Erb, Joh. dicto Arnoltz, V oI. dicto Lesti, Joh. dicto Ergger, V oI. Hospite, .. dicto Ko efil, V oI. Cibusse, H. filio suo, C. dicto Wiennehter, Joh. dic to Spete, C. dicto Stre af et aliis quam pluribus fidedignis.

Siegel: Siegel an blauen Fäden, Abb. 112.
entries.english:
Abbot Heinrich of St. Gallen grants Ulrich von Gmünden, his wife, and their children the burgher right of the city of St. Gallen.

In the name of the Lord, amen. Heinrich, by God's grace abbot of the monastery of St. Gallen, wishes salvation in the Lord and knowledge of the following to all who see this document. Let all who need to know understand that, in consideration of the valued devout services which the prudent man Ulrich von Gmünden has rendered to us and our monastery, and strives still to render, we have granted him, as a favor for these services, and by this letter give and bestow upon him, Mehtild his wife, daughter of Heinrich, formerly ministerial at Tüfen, Bersin their son, and all children they may henceforth have together, the full right of burghership or citizenship in our town of St. Gallen, commonly called our burgher right, with all rights, liberties, and the area encompassed by that designation. We will that the aforementioned Ulrich, his wife Mehtild, their son Bersin, and all their children of either sex enjoy and use this same right and custom, as established by our predecessors and in former times, and observed inviolate until now. In good faith, on behalf of ourselves and all our successors, we promise to protect these persons in every respect in this burgher right, both in life and in death. In witness of this we have caused our seal to be affixed to this document. Given and enacted at St. Gallen in the year of the Lord 1304, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of September. Present were Lord Eglolf von Rosenberg; Walther of Enwil; Volrich called Meldeli; V., the town minister of St. Gallen; Wilderich and his son Volrich; Albrecht called Blarrer, C. called Blarrer, H. called Blarrer; C., minister of Appenzell; H. called Erb; John called Arnoltz; Volrich called Lesti; John called Ergger; Volrich Hospite; ... called Koefil; Volrich Cibusse and his son H.; C. called Wiennehter; John called Spete; C. called Streaf; and many other trustworthy people.

Seal: attached by blue threads; illustration 112.
